title: Moon base: the 354-hour night (restart, all made 3D)
note: Every sentence comes from the goal's facts in the app (bottlenecks b3.1, b3.3, b2.5 for the temperature shown, and the pending promise 'NASA astronauts would visit the Moon's south pole by 2030'). Every shot is made 3D of the goal's own subject; nothing real is inserted. Shots: s1x the habitat at night (night_video.py SHOT 3), s2x the sunlight sweep (pole_light.py), s3x a far ridge losing sunlight (SHOT 7), s4 a person at the habitat (SHOT 2), s5x the orbiter (lro_pass.py), s6x the glide toward Shackleton crater (lro_pass.py NOCRAFT), s7 the empty ridge (SHOT 6), s8 the astronaut in sunlight (SHOT 5).

shots.job: This shot shows a lit habitat at night with the hours counting up, so the viewer understands how long one night is for a base.
This shot shows a month of sunlight sweeping the south pole as the count reaches 354, so the viewer sees the number against the place.
This shot shows the last sunlight leaving a far ridge as the temperature falls, so the viewer understands why machines shut down.
This shot shows a person outside the lit habitat in the dark, so the viewer understands what cannot be switched off.
This shot shows the orbiter whose terrain measurements the sunlight study rests on, with the study named, so the viewer knows on what evidence the claim stands.
This shot shows the ridge itself, named, with its year of sunlight drawn as a strip, so the viewer sees the dark spells the line speaks of.
This shot shows the ridge empty under the night sky, so the viewer sees that nobody has done it yet.
This shot shows an astronaut on that ridge in sunlight with Earth beyond, so the viewer sees what has been promised.

lines.say: A Moon base would face nights about three hundred and fifty-four hours long.
text: A Moon base would face nights

lines.say: Small landers have survived them by mostly shutting down.
Some ridges at the south pole get sunlight most of the time.
